label: Cisco GLC-ZX-SMD 1000BASE-ZX 80 km
notes: Cisco SFP and SFP+ Transceiver Module Installation Notes, Table 5 (1-Gigabit SFP optical transmit and receive specifications), rows GLC-ZX-SM / GLC-ZX-SM-RGD / SFP-GE-Z / GLC-ZX-SMD: average transmit power 0..+5 dBm, receive power -3 (max) .. -23 (min) dBm, 1500-1580 nm, 43.4-62 miles (70-100 km) on G.652 - so 0 - (-23) = 23 dB between the launch floor and the sensitivity floor. This row carried -24 dBm until 2026-11-24, and no document it cited printed that figure: -24 is a common third-party ZX-compatible claim, and it handed every 1000BASE-ZX link 1 dB that had not been sold. Take -24 from the module actually bought if its test report prints it; the catalogue row keeps the figure its own sourceUrl publishes. 1000BASE-ZX is NOT an IEEE 802.3 class - ZX is a vendor long-reach convention - so this row cites the vendor rather than a standard, and must not be read as a class limit. The two verdicts sit 1 dB apart in opposite directions. Loss: 80 km of G.652.D at 0.21 dB/km is 16.8 dB, which leaves 6.2 dB of the 23 for every splice, connector and the default 3 dB margin - a measured 80 km run with five splices and two connector pairs reads 5.1 dB of headroom. Overload: at the +5 dBm launch ceiling the receiver's -3 dBm maximum is 8 dB below it, and Cisco states that same 8 dB as the minimum attenuation between the transmit and receive bores, so any span shorter than about 38 km (8 / 0.21) needs a pad - the budget's attenuator verdict names it, and more reach is never the answer. The 80 km in the model name is the middle of Cisco's 70-100 km declaration, not a published reach: the loss budget refuses a long run before the distance does. Replace these figures with the test report for the module actually purchased before pricing a build.
